description.narrative: The Yemen Joint Response is a 3-year project funded by the Dutch Ministry of Foreign Affairs through the Dutch Relief Alliance. It focuses on short-term and longer-term needs in Lahj and Marib. It encompasses multiple sectors, including emergency food security and livelihoods, protection and WASH. It supports vulnerable people in restoring and improving their livelihoods and creating income opportunities to build their resilience in order to cope with the impacts of the ongoing crises as both locations are faced with complex and multi-dimensional humanitarian challenges, including displacement and high levels of food insecurity. Priorities include thedistribution of cash grants for businesses, establishing community-based protection networks, rehabilitation of water supply systems and hygiene promotion activities. As part of this project, Oxfam in Yemen is partnering with two Yemeni organisations.

participating-org.narrative: Oxfam is an international confederation of 17 organizations working together in more than 90 countries. Oxfam International was formed in 1995 by a group of independent non-governmental organizations. Their aim was to work together for greater impact on the international stage to reduce poverty and injustice. The name "Oxfam" comes from the Oxford Committee for Famine Relief, founded in Britain in 1942. The group campaigned for food supplies to be sent through an allied naval blockade to starving women and children in enemy-occupied Greece during the Second World War. As well as becoming a world leader in the delivery of emergency relief, Oxfam International implements long-term development programs in vulnerable communities. We are also part of a global movement, campaigning with others, for instance, to end unfair trade rules, demand better health and education services for all, and to combat climate change. Today, there are 17 member organizations of the Oxfam International confederation. They are based in: Australia, Belgium, Canada,France, Germany, Great Britain, Hong Kong, Ireland, India, Italy, Japan, Mexico, The Netherlands, New Zealand, Quebec, Spain and the United States. The Oxfam International Secretariat is based in Oxford, UK. The Secretariat runs advocacy offices in Brussels, Geneva, New York, Washington DC and Brasilia. Oxfam GB is an actor in the implementation of this project.

comment.narrative: "in lahj Training was held for 18 CBPNs (9 males, 9 females), 5 MOSAL case managers (2 males, 3 females), and 4 local authorities. The training will focus on the targeted district and engage existing actors to ensure the promotion of their capacities in supporting and referring protection cases to relevant services. "

comment.narrative: Oxfam plans to support the sanitation fund by providing a 12 m³ suction truck to help the HIF remove wastewater from cesspits in five IDP camps in Marib city. A three-year agreement was signed with HIF, which will cover operational costs. However, all tender offers exceeded the allocated budget, leading to negotiations with HIF and Oxfam’s management to address the shortfall, causing delays. In the meantime, Oxfam has continued desludging cesspits in the targeted camps through other projects like SIDA and OUS.

comment.narrative: "The Al-Khasha Water Project was selected for intervention after coordination with the WASH cluster and GRWAP. It features an artesian well donated by a philanthropist, but the original pump was damaged due to direct pumping into the water network. A temporary pump was rented, but the water tower had been out of service for 12 years due to severe damage.Oxfam completed the rehabilitation by providing a new 20-kilowatt pump, repairing the water tower, and reconnecting it to the pumping and distribution lines. As a result, 450 households/3150 individuals (including IDPs and host community members) now have access to sufficient water. A water management committee was established and trained in system operation, maintenance, and chlorination, with maintenance and water quality kits distributed to support ongoing monitoring and treatmentcrisis modifier : 01 water scheme were provided with submersible pump to access safe water in cholera affected areas. 250 HHs/1750 individuals were benefited from this activity through cirse modifier -Oxfam in Alsamadah IDPs camp in Marib AL wadi.
